diary.id: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers-2002-2026-07-17
diary.Name: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
diary.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
diary.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
diary.Review:
The Two Towers is still an absolute masterpiece with way more pros than cons. It has everything going for it, the world design is gorgeous, the score is epic, and the defense of Helm’s Deep is easily one of the coolest battles in cinema. Plus, watching Frodo and Sam learn how to survive in the wild, and seeing Merry and Pippin rally the Ents to fight back, is just awesome to watch.

But for me, juggling so many storylines at once actually hurts the movie's intensity. I get that the film is trying to create a massive sense of urgency by showing everything happening at the exact same time. The problem is that it constantly puts off the climax of each section. It’s a bit weird to be thrown from the high-stakes, epic energy of Helm’s Deep right into the slow-moving morals of the Ents. That abrupt shift in tone makes it hard to stay totally locked in.

Overall, it’s still a great movie, but the fragmented pacing just holds it back a little.

diary.Name: Loving Vincent
diary.name: Loving Vincent
diary.title: Loving Vincent
diary.Review:
I have never written a review on note before, but i wanted to show how much i felt for this movie but here is my honest thought and review of the movie Loving Vincent (2017):

If you strip away the formal detective framework of Loving Vincent, you are left with something far more profound: a post-mortem diary of isolation, told entirely through the fractured recollections of the people who crossed the artist’s path. It is a collective eulogy for a soul that vanished into his own canvas.

What makes this film bypass the intellect and strike the heart so directly is its staggering visual dissonance. We never see a single physical canvas hanging on a gallery wall, instead, the entire universe is his canvas. 

The film immerses us in his thick, swirling brushstrokes and vibrant palettes, yet the man at the center of it is deteriorating into a small, fragile, and intensely burdened existence. His final, devastating comfort to Dr. Gachet after being shot "It's maybe the best for everyone" is a crushing portrayal of deep-rooted despair. It strips away the romanticism of the "tortured artist" and forces you to confront the raw reality of severe mental illness, where a person genuinely convinces themselves that their absence is a gift to the ones they love.

But the film's ultimate masterstroke is its manipulation of color. Throughout the runtime, the flashbacks of Vincent are rendered strictly in cold, muted black-and-white. It is a heartbreaking reflection of how he actually experienced his own life—trapped in a monochrome of loneliness and perceived failure, entirely blind to the immense color he was giving to the world.

It is only in the very final moments, as the film transitions out of the narrative, that we are allowed to see Vincent in full, vibrant color. It is a paradigm shift that occurs entirely in the eyes of the viewer and the legacy of the people left behind. In that final exhale, we finally see him not as a tragic shadow, but as he truly was: that red-haired, slim Dutch man who simply loved to paint the world.

When the swirling patterns of Starry Night finally align with the closing music, it ceases to be a technical experiment. It becomes an overwhelming emotional weight that demands you stop whatever you are doing, step back, and sit in the quiet aftermath of its crushing beauty.

diary.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
diary.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
diary.Review:
Accidentally watched the extended cut for my first viewing and holy crap, what an absolute masterpiece.
For a movie from 2001, the effects and gorgeous environmental design is such a treat to see.

The world-building is next-level, but it’s the character depth and incredible acting that keep you hooked, tie it all together with Howard Shore's legendary, heroic score that makes everything feel massive, and it's obvious why this is rated so high.

Though being the first movie of course most of the story is going to be about the introductions of the characters and races and the world, so it feels quite slow.

diary.Review: Absolutely heartbreaking performance from Sir Anthony Hopkins, very strong and indifferent portrayal of a character in this adult doomed love theme, its the movie of not saying enough or being too late, how a person who holds themselves in one place or position for too long, can only be nothing without it, i really enjoyed this, with its subplots in the background really surprised me on how intricate and deep this story was, theres many scenes where we just stop and stare at Sir Anthony's blue eyes, and i really felt like they were pale, empty, and had nothing behind them, like stevens the butler was the only thing here, not james, jim, or anything else but just this empty armor of a dutiful servant working for this manor of darkness.

diary.Review: some movies make you think about what you have done in your life, this was a quite heartbreaking film about mental health, grief and memories, i really liked how the strobing lights show how a faded memory sophie has of her father, and i liked the non linear storytelling, makes me think that this was because of how memories work, you remember things sometimes not chronologically, but how much it made an impact in your life, and thats why this movie felt like it was fading away, stripping itself bit by bit, sometimes we stop and pause for a minute or two, its like sophie is trying to remember slowly and i really think that this was a beautiful film on silent grief, Paul Mescal is absolutely phenomenal.

diary.name: A Ghost Story
diary.title: A Ghost Story
diary.Review:
This movie felt like a memory of someone trying to remember their life, but it was going away, fading.

A movie full of subtleties, very slow and patient, it feels more like a meditation of sorrow and regret, rather than an emotional grief movie to me, its beautiful how it was shot, the score was eerie and suspenseful, I don't think much people would watch this movie, because of its very slow pace and near zero dialogue, but It's a good metaphor on how keeping regrets and how to not stay too much in the past.

diary.Review: At the first 1 hour of the movie, I wasn't really feeling the acting of this movie, the characters seemed abit laidback and sort of passive, for a periodic war film, it didnt feel like everyone was on edge or more aggressive in how they view the war, but after Marcus was killed, the tone of the movie changed, Maximus and Commodus were both transformed, where Maximus took Marcus's stoic and calm nature, and Commodus took the sly, and deceiving parts of the senate, it really opened my eye on how Russel crowe won the Oscar, he wasn't portraying a Blood thirsty, tyrannical general but more of a philosophical and stern approach of a leader, and he hit it perfectly to me, with amazing supporting actors, the great cinematography, and a real good pick for the best picture award.

diary.Name: The Shawshank Redemption
diary.name: The Shawshank Redemption
diary.title: The Shawshank Redemption
diary.Review:
I watched this film when I was younger because I wanted to see all the hype about why it was the highest rated movie on imdb, growing older and post a 5 or so years of watching movies passively, I thought about rewatching it with a clearer mind, and more focus and appreciation on the performances, cinematography, score, and symbolism on all films.

Shawshank Redemption struck me as a film not really about prison life or prison escapes, it felt more of a version of purgatory for Andy, how he had to work for 20 years, being beaten, scammed, and extorted till an inch of his life, he gone through that, and his quote "Get busy living, or Get busy dying", was really an encapsulation on his life, cause we started with his life destroyed, being accused of murdering his own wife, being sentenced to 2 life sentences, it felt as if he was more busy dying, and how I saw it when he crawled through the shit tunnel, he came out of hell, and descended as a free man or a free spirit.

This was an amazing movie, amazing camera work with lots of boxed in perspectives, the score is remarkable, couldn't look away when you have such great scores in the background, great experience of sadness, joy, humor, and hope.

diary.name: Hamnet
diary.title: Hamnet
diary.Review:
How can one truly love, knowing that grief will eventually follow?
How can a person still live after losing a loved one?

Some couldn't;
some persevere, only to flame out.

But then there are those who are eternalized
remembered for generations,
living on as art, as pieces of history,
and to some, as a light.

Anxiety filled, Visually Breathtaking and Despairing in every second.

Oh what a curse it is to experience love,

diary.name: Once We Were Us
diary.title: Once We Were Us
diary.Review:
I went into this film thinking it was something like past lives, and it mostly was, but with more focus on the two main leads, it explored both of their upbringing quite subtly, not really digging much into their past all that much, but they did a good job giving both of the leads enough background and individual stories for it to be a grounded relationship and understand their own point of view on life and how the relationship went.

Technically the movie wasn't anything special, nice colors, good camera work, good dialogue and nice supporting characters, on any other day watching this in the middle of the day on my laptop, it probably wouldn't make me feel much of anything, but watching this in an empty theater at night, with no one else but me, I felt immersed into the story, laughing, smiling and being emotional by myself, it forced me to be in the moment not opening my phone and seeing how they progressed into the eventual parting.

I really loved the scenes with the father, it really showed different sides of both characters, but, I cried watching this, it really felt more intense being alone not being able to share this emotions with somebody, and I kinda understood what they felt, just a little bit, I recommend anyone to give this a watch with your loved one, a friend, or a stranger, cause it may not be an amazing life changing movie, or a technical marvel, the story is not even that groundbreaking, I think it's a movie where if you watch it in the right moment, you'll find yourself getting your heart strings abit tugged.

diary.Review:
In a trilogy of amazing movies, there will be always one that wasn't as good as the others but still great, though being roughly the same amount of time as blue, this one felt very grounded, where blue really focused on the internal part of life, where it used the blue color to exemplify grief or sadness with these booming orchestras playing, where in white it felt more like an old drama you'd see on tv in the morning's, it was slow, soothing, comedic, but gave you a quite bitter feeling in the end, how we see the struggle of Karol after divorce, going through Post-communist Poland, with this beautiful relationship of Karol and Mikolaj.

This movie kinda felt out of place, with how thematically the color white was used, it was not as much of a focal point as it was in blue, where white here was used to give the feeling of emptiness, this pure shining unattainable memory of Karol, all in all, it was a great movie and I can't wait to see red.

diary.Review:
It would be hard to describe to people what this film is actually about, because it is for one a 3 hour foreign movie that was made 26 years ago, I understand how people might feel a bit overwhelmed to see what is all the importance of this film, I felt that way as well at first and kept putting this movie off for a long while, this movie was really an in-depth showing of complex emotions, like NJ's long lasting regret with his old lover, or the curiosity of life by Yang-Yang's camerawork.

It would be an understatement to say that this was just a slice of life family drama, cause there wasn't any together happy ending, it was this bittersweet ending of grief from the family and Yang-Yang's Monologue really gave me a more understanding on how his Grandma was in their family's lives.

if you ever watch this movie, I recommend you to fully watch it, because its going to be slow, drawn out, a lot of silent wide shots, and near minimal dialogue at some points.

diary.Review: There's something beautiful about seeing a family that was strained in the beginning to near breaking apart, and end with a sliver of hope still tying them together, this movie did pretty good at exploring each family member's perspective on dealing with their troubles and how they face them, I would have preferred to see more of takashi, but all in all this film had some great camera work, some of the scenes that stood out was the silence when the father found out that his buddy died, and when the mother sat on the beach sitting on the shore, and especially the ending where it was a 5 minute still shot of Kenji playing Clair de lune, all In all it was an interesting take on family matters and soul searching.
